reason: This text fragment (Exodus 5-11) does not depict Yahweh as angry when hearing the people voice their opinions and feelings. When Moses voices his complaint to Yahweh—'Lord, why have you dealt ill with this people? Why did you send me?'—Yahweh responds with reassurance and a plan of action ('Now you will see what I will do to Pharaoh, for with a strong hand he will let them go'), not with anger. The Israelite slaves do voice their suffering and complaints to their supervisors and indirectly to Moses and Aaron, but there is no record of Yahweh expressing anger at them for doing so. Yahweh's anger in this passage is directed at Pharaoh for refusing to release the people, which prompts the plagues. The passage demonstrates Yahweh as responsive and compassionate to the people's distress, not angry at their expressions of hardship.
